name: English
meta: Areopagus: a European network of real people. Built in the open, together.
kicker: A European network of real people
lead: Areopagus gives everyone a page, every town a map and every person a voice. No ads, open code. The network is only starting, and you can build it with us.
stationText: Areopagus is also a legend: an orbital station that all of humanity builds. It is named after the hill in Athens where the apostle Paul spoke with the philosophers in their own language (Acts 17). Cargo ships carry everything for the building up from the Earth, and anyone can send cargo. The crew of the station are Christians, and they serve the common work: they meet on board to agree on the affairs of the Earth and go back to work below, so that the Earth becomes a garden for all who live on it.
stationVerse: Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven
earthText: Open to everyone. Each person has a space for earthly things: a page, a home port, skills, a logbook, questions, communities. Everyone can see what the station does and where it is heading.
aboardText: The station is the home of the crew, Christians who serve the common work. The way aboard is being prepared and will be published after a legal review. The station takes a person at their word and does not judge anyone's faith.
stationNote: The picture is close to how such a station could really be built: two rings with a radius of 250 m turn in opposite directions at 1.9 turns a minute, which gives the weight we have on Earth, 800 km above it. One ring is always being built.
pathText: What is done is lit. What is in work pulses. What is planned is an outline. No dates here, only an honest order.
nodes: A legal home for the project
joinText: Nobody is ranked here. Every release names all who had a hand in it, in alphabetical order.
ways: Add an idea. It appears on the path as an outline next to its branch.
One voice per person per idea. Numbers belong to ideas, never to people.
Translation, testing on your phone, data about your town, code.
Join the circle that gets new things before everyone else.
For one step of the path or for keeping the network running.
supText: One number matters: until which month the network is paid for. For now the project is run by its founder as a sole trader in France, so support is his business income, not a charitable gift.
rules: Every euro in and every euro out goes into a public journal anyone can verify.
A donation buys no voting weight, no placement and no badge.
Your name is shown only if you ask for it.
engText: Areopagus is also an engine. Your space, shop or community can live on your own domain by subscription. The code is open, so anyone may run it themselves for free.
foot: Open code under AGPL. Data in Europe. No ads, ever.

legend.title: The legend of the station
legend.meta: How an orbital station that all of humanity builds got its name from a hill in Athens, told in eight pictures.
legend.lead: Areopagus is named after a hill in Athens where, around AD 50, the apostle Paul spoke with the philosophers in their own language. Here is that story and what the station takes from it.

ch.p: Next to the Acropolis rises a bare rock, the hill of Ares. The oldest council of Athens met there and took its name from it: the Areopagus. In Roman times it still watched over what was taught in the city.
ch.alt: Engraving: the Acropolis and its temples seen from the hill of Ares, the city below.

ch.p: Paul was waiting in Athens for his companions. The city was full of idols, and it troubled him. Every day he talked in the synagogue and in the market square with whoever was there. Epicurean and Stoic philosophers argued with him. Some called him a babbler, in Greek a seed picker, someone who pecks up scraps of other people's ideas. They took him to the Areopagus and asked:
ch.q: May we know what this new teaching is, which you are speaking about?
ch.alt: Engraving: the market square of Athens with a long colonnade, herms and statues, the Acropolis above.

ch.p: Paul did not begin by accusing them. He began with what they already had. Walking through the city he had found an altar with the inscription ΑΓΝΩΣΤΩ ΘΕΩ, to an unknown god.
ch.q: What therefore you worship in ignorance, I announce to you.
ch.alt: Engraving: a marble altar with a Greek inscription to an unknown god, a colonnade behind it.

ch.p: He spoke of the God who made the world and does not live in temples made by hands, who is not far from each one of us. He quoted their own poets: in him we live and move and have our being; we are his offspring. That second line comes from Aratus, a poet from Cilicia, Paul's home country.
ch.q: He made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the surface of the earth
ch.alt: Engraving: a globe with Europe, Africa and Asia, Athens marked with a ring.

ch.p: Paul ended with a call to turn to God and spoke of the man whom God raised from the dead. At the word resurrection the listeners split. Some mocked. Others said:
ch.q: We want to hear you again concerning this.
ch.a: Some believed, among them Dionysius, a member of the council, and a woman named Damaris. Tradition says Dionysius became the first bishop of Athens.
ch.alt: Engraving: night on the hill of Ares, the Acropolis dark against the moon.

ch.p: Areopagus is also the name of an orbital station that all of humanity builds. Everything for the building comes up from the Earth on cargo ships, and anyone can send cargo: code, a contribution, a translation, an observation of their own place.
ch.alt: The station above the Alps and Italy, cargo ships on their way to it.

ch.p: The crew of the station are Christians. They meet under the dome to agree on the affairs of the Earth, then go back down to work. Here to lead means to serve.
ch.q: But it shall not be so among you, but whoever wants to become great among you shall be your servant.
ch.alt: The domed hall of the station with lit windows, a cargo ship arriving.

ch.p: The station is not built for its own sake. The aim is that the Earth becomes a garden for all who live on it.
ch.q: Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven
ch.alt: The station, small, above the curve of the Earth in daylight.

legend.wordsTitle: Words of Jesus, rules of the station

words.q: Even so, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
words.rule: The logbook is open: everyone can see what the station does.

words.q: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, doesn't first sit down and count the cost, to see if he has enough to complete it?
words.rule: The station does not spend more than it brings up.

words.q: By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.
words.rule: The crew is known by how its members treat one another.

legend.credits: Pictures made in Blender for Areopagus; the old scenes are engraved from the same models. Earth: NASA Earth Observatory. Scripture: World English Bible, public domain.
